steps.title: Import fetch API and create main function
steps.instruction: Create a function named getWeatherData that will fetch weather information. This function should be declared with the async keyword since it will make an API call.
steps.hint: Start with 'async function getWeatherData() {}' or 'const getWeatherData = async () => {}' to create an asynchronous function.
steps.seedCode: // Create your async getWeatherData function here
steps.expectedOutcome: An async function named getWeatherData is created and ready to contain fetch logic.
successCriteria: Function getWeatherData is declared with async keyword and has an empty body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main async function that will handle weather data fetching.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created an async function named getWeatherData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that you used the async keyword and named it getWeatherData.

steps.title: Create HTML structure with container elements
steps.instruction: Create a container div element with the class 'weather-dashboard' that will wrap all the dashboard sections.
steps.hint:

successCriteria: The WeatherDashboard function returns a div element with className='weather-dashboard'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container for the weather dashboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're returning a div with the correct class name.

steps.title: Initialize state variables for weather data
steps.instruction: Inside the WeatherDashboard function, declare three variables using let: currentWeather, forecast, and isLoading. Initialize each with null.
steps.hint: You'll need to declare these variables at the top of your function before the return statement. Use let variableName = null;
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function will have three variables ready to store weather data and loading state.
successCriteria: The WeatherDashboard function contains three let declarations: currentWeather, forecast, and isLoading, each initialized with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created variables to store weather data and loading state. These will be used to hold API responses and track when data is being fetched.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared all three variables: currentWeather, forecast, and isLoading. Each should be initialized with null using let.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the WeatherDashboard function, declare three variables using let: currentWeather, forecast, and isLoading. Initialize each with null.

steps.title: Create search input and button elements
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your WeatherDashboard component, add an input field with placeholder text 'Enter city name' and a button with text 'Search'.
steps.hint: Add the input and button elements inside the container div. Use the placeholder attribute for the input and put the button text between its tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard UI now includes a search input field and a search button inside the container div.
successCriteria: The return statement contains an input element with placeholder='Enter city name' and a button element with text 'Search'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the search input and button. Users can now enter a city name to search for weather data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both an input with placeholder text 'Enter city name' and a button with text 'Search'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The search controls aren't complete. Add an input field with placeholder text 'Enter city name' and a button with text 'Search' inside the container div.

steps.title: Define function to fetch weather data from API
steps.instruction: Inside the WeatherDashboard component, create an async function named getWeatherData that takes a city parameter and uses fetch to get weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API.
steps.hint: Use the fetch API with the OpenWeatherMap endpoint (e.g., https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q={city}&appid={API_KEY}). Remember to use async/await and handle the response with .json().
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async getWeatherData function that uses fetch to retrieve weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API.
successCriteria: The getWeatherData function is defined inside the WeatherDashboard component, is async, takes a city parameter, uses fetch with the OpenWeatherMap API endpoint, and returns the parsed JSON data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the async function that will fetch weather data from the API.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is async, uses fetch with the correct API endpoint, and properly handles the response with .json().
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to be defined correctly. Remember to create an async function named getWeatherData that uses fetch to call the OpenWeatherMap API.

steps.title: Create function to handle search button click
steps.instruction: Inside the WeatherDashboard component, create a function named handleSearch that will call your getWeatherData function when the search button is clicked.
steps.hint: Define a regular function inside your component that calls getWeatherData. You don't need to pass any arguments yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSearch function is defined inside the WeatherDashboard component that will trigger the weather data fetch.
successCriteria: The handleSearch function is created and calls getWeatherData inside its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handleSearch function that will trigger the weather fetch when the search button is clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleSearch function actually calls getWeatherData inside its body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleSearch inside the WeatherDashboard component that calls getWeatherData.

steps.title: Wire search button to click handler
steps.instruction: Add an onClick event handler to the search button that calls your handleSearch function.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on the button element and set it equal to your handleSearch function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an event handler to a button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The search button will now trigger the handleSearch function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has an onClick attribute set to handleSearch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the search button to your click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added onClick={handleSearch} to the button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs an onClick event handler that calls the handleSearch function.

steps.expectedOutcome: A displayCurrentWeather function is created that will be used to update the UI with weather data.

steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a container div with class 'forecast-container' after the current weather display. Inside this container, create three div elements with class 'forecast-card' as placeholders for forecast days.

steps.title: Add error handling and loading states
steps.instruction: Inside your WeatherDashboard component, add a loading state variable and an error state variable to track API request status.
steps.hint: You can declare two new state variables using let or const, for example: let isLoading = false; and let error = null;
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two new variables to track loading and error states, which will later be used to show feedback to users.
successCriteria: The component contains a loading state variable and an error state variable declared inside the WeatherDashboard function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the state variables needed for error handling and loading indicators. These will help provide better user feedback during API calls.
